a multi-protein biomarker panel, including osteocalin, osteomodulins, and collagen alpha 1(v), may provide a solution to detect and monitor HO.
a multi-protein assay panel, including osteocalin preprotein, osteo-modulin precursor, and type I collagen, may be a solution for HO diagnosis and monitoring.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of potential serum biomarkers for HO.
the development of a proteomic-based biomarker panel that may be useful in the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of HO.
the identification of novel serum biomarkers of HO and the potential for a serum biomarker assay to be developed for clinical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study is the first to use SRM-MS to analyze the serum of individuals with and without HO, and the results show that the serum proteomic profiles differ significantly between healthy and diseasing subjects.

the proteomic profile of serum from patients suffering from heterotopic ossifications is significantly different from healthy individuals and that a panel of three proteins, osteocalcium preproprotein, collagen alpha- 1(v) chain preprotein isoform 2 and osteomodulin are potential candidates for a diagnostic panel for heterotopic osteosynthesis.
this study is the first proteomic study of heterotopic ossifications in blood serum and the first study to use SRM-MS to analyze blood serum from individuals with heterotopic ossifaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteomics data generated in this study provides a framework for future biomarker development, and the three proteins identified as potential biomarkers are worthy of future investigation.
the use of iTRAQ and SRM-MS can be used to identify potential biomarkers and that the combination of these two techniques is a powerful tool in the identification of biomarkers.
a multi-protein biomarker panel for heterotopic bone formation has been developed, and this assay is ready for further clinical evaluation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteomic signature of serum is a complex mixture of proteins that are influenced by the health of the patient.

a proteomic approach to biomarker discovery is a promising approach, but the proteomics field must develop more sophisticated statistical methods and bioinformatics tools for the analysis of proteomic data.

the use of proteomics to identify biomarkers of heterotopic ossificans is feasible, but it will require careful consideration of the patient cohort, the timing of the blood draw, and the use of a multi-protein biomarker panel.
